title: UI Mockups in Docs and Plans

text.insert: This spec proposes UI mockups as a component that specs, plans, and design docs can embed. An agent writes each screen as a semantic HTML fragment plus a surface preset, and the docs renderer owns the frame, theme, and sketch styling. Reviewers see the screens beside the prose and annotate individual controls. The page compares three ways to fit mockups into the block vocabulary and recommends a staged path.
Proposed and non-normative. Nothing on this page is built. Every type, tool, and lint rule named here as new is a proposal.
Specs and plans in this corpus describe user-facing screens only in prose. A reviewer cannot see the proposed screen, compare its states, or point at one control.
A paragraph that describes a panel hides its layout decisions until implementation, when changing them costs the most.
can hold a mockup, but the author writes every color, font, and frame. Mockups then differ from page to page and break in dark mode.
targets a block, a text range, or a canvas object. It cannot target one button inside a rendered screen.

The Agent-Native visual plan generated from the agent-kernel Model Nodes spec shows the alternative. Its top canvas holds three trace-viewer screens with designer notes, so a reviewer reads the UI before the prose.
The board below shows the target reading experience for a small review panel. It is hand-built with today's
block, so its author wrote every color and font. That cost is what this spec removes.

props.title: Integration options compared

text.insert: A new block type stores one screen in props and renders it through the sandbox that
already uses. It ships with no change outside docs-system.
Screens stack in reading order, so a page cannot lay states side by side or park notes in a gutter.
A screen becomes one canvas object, so it sits in sections beside notes and connectors and is edited with the existing
tools. This option matches the reference board most closely.
The canvas type set is closed in
. A screen therefore needs a schema change and a new render path in the canvas package.
A spec or plan page gains a fixed top area with Wireframes and Prototype tabs, as in the reference. The area adds a second layout model to every page that uses it.
A canvas block placed first on the page gives the same reading order. The block already renders inline and opens a full-screen viewer.
Build one screen model and one renderer, then host it twice. Ship it first as the inline
object kind to canvas boards second (B). Treat the page review area (C) as a page convention.
The shared part costs the most
The stylesheet, lint rules, and node anchors are the same in both hosts. The inline block proves them without touching the canvas package.
The board reuses canvas instead of rebuilding it
Option B gets sections, connectors, notes, the typed edit tools, and layout lints from the canvas package. A mockup-only board would duplicate all five.
The review area needs no new surface
A spec with UI opens with its mockup canvas, and the agent guidance states that convention. A prototype tab waits for a real need.
The recommendation needs one screen schema, two authoring tools, a renderer contract, lint rules, and agent guidance. Every name in this section is proposed.

props.title: Mockup phases

text.insert: Clickable prototypes, a page-level tab surface, Figma import or export, and pixel comparison against built UI stay deferred until a spec needs them.
Four choices become expensive to change once documents and annotations depend on them. Each one is settled here before Phase 1.
A block keeps its screen in props, so the screen shares the doc hash, undo, and diff, as the
On a board the screen is one object inside the canvas sidecar. A separate mockup sidecar would add a third authority and a third forwarding path.
Content is HTML, not a node tree
The reference still renders a legacy kit tree of components, but it authors every new screen as HTML.
HTML uses layout skills agents already have. Lint enforces the limits that a closed node schema would otherwise enforce.
breaks when a sibling is inserted. An authored
survives edits the way block ids do.
The anchor is an optional field on existing targets, so the annotation schema grows additively and old sidecars stay valid.
The schema lives in the canvas package
, and the canvas package does not depend on docs-model. Exporting
from the canvas package lets both hosts validate one shape.
Each question carries a recommended default, so Phase 1 can start before it is answered.
Is sketch styling the default on docs pages?
Recommended default is yes, matching the reference. The sketch signals that a screen is a proposal and not a capture of shipped UI.
until a prototype phase defines navigation.
Which package owns the stylesheet and tokens?
Recommended default is the canvas package, beside the schema. Its
values derive from the docs theme and from the three canvas themes.
How does the static board export draw a screen?
Recommended default is a labeled frame in the SVG, with the live iframe overlaid only by the interactive viewer. This keeps
Are mockups limited to the specs tier?
Recommended default is no. System design pages can show UI states with the same block.
